items.followUp: Define an ionic bond and write four properties of ionic compounds.

rubric.why: A covalent bond forms when atoms share electron pairs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining it as a bond formed by sharing one or more pairs of electrons between atoms.

rubric.why: Covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.

rubric.why: Covalent compounds generally lack mobile charged particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that covalent compounds generally do not conduct electricity.

rubric.why: The solubility pattern is a characteristic property of many covalent compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they are generally insoluble in water or soluble in organic solvents.

rubric.why: Many covalent compounds are gases, liquids, or soft solids at room temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that covalent compounds are often gases, liquids, or soft solids at room temperature.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is a chemical bond formed when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
Covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.
They generally do not conduct electricity.
Many are insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents.
They are often gases, liquids, or soft solids at room temperature.

items.followUp: How many particles are present in one mole of a substance? Give the name and value of this number.

rubric.why: The definition identifies the number of particles in one mole.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining Avogadro's number as the number of particles or entities in one mole of a substance.

rubric.why: The value is the key quantitative fact in the definition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the value as approximately 6.02 × 10²³.

modelAnswer: Avogadro's number is the number of particles present in one mole of a substance.
